prompts.usageInstructions: Bring your journal on every outdoor walk, even just to the park.

prompts.title: Water Garden and Pond Setup Guide
prompts.description: Create a tranquil backyard water feature.
prompts.text: Write a backyard water garden setup guide for [Name] with [Available Space]. Options covered: container water garden (for small spaces), pre-formed pond kits, and natural wildlife pond. For each: liner/container choice, plant selection (lotus, water hyacinth, oxygenating plants), fish compatibility, maintenance schedule, and mosquito prevention strategies.
prompts.usageInstructions: Site the pond in a location with at least 6 hours of sunlight.

prompts.title: Eco-Friendly Pest Control for Gardens
prompts.description: Control garden pests without harmful chemicals.
prompts.text: Write an eco-friendly pest control guide for [Name]'s garden dealing with [Pest Issue: aphids/whitefly/slugs/caterpillars]. Cover: natural predators to attract, DIY organic sprays (neem oil, garlic spray, chilli spray), physical barriers, trap cropping, and companion planting solutions. Include a "first signs" identification guide for early intervention.
prompts.usageInstructions: Identify the pest correctly before applying any treatment.

prompts.title: Moon Phase Gardening Calendar
prompts.description: Plant and harvest in harmony with the lunar cycle.
prompts.text: Create a moon phase gardening calendar guide for [Name] for the next 3 months. Explain the biodynamic gardening principle (root days, leaf days, fruit days, flower days). For each lunar phase (new, waxing crescent, first quarter, full, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent, dark moon), specify ideal gardening tasks and a sample schedule for [Month].
prompts.usageInstructions: Unlock and pair with a biodynamic lunar calendar app.

prompts.title: Funny Birthday Roast for a Sibling
prompts.description: A loving roast for your brother or sister.
prompts.text: Write a hilarious birthday roast for my [brother/sister] [Name] turning [Age]. Reference their most embarrassing habits: [Habit1] and [Habit2]. Start with a fake compliment, escalate to a roast, then end with a sweet, genuine 2-sentence love note that shows it's all in good fun. Keep it G-rated but hilariously accurate.
prompts.usageInstructions: Read aloud at the birthday dinner for maximum effect.

prompts.title: Passive-Aggressive Office Note (Humorous)
prompts.description: A funny note for the office kitchen thief.
prompts.text: Write 5 hilariously passive-aggressive but office-appropriate notes about [Office Issue: lunch stealing/unwashed dishes/loud phone calls]. Each note should be funny enough that even the guilty party would laugh, but clear enough to change the behaviour. Include a sign-off like "Regards, The Entire Office".
prompts.usageInstructions: Post in the relevant area and watch the guilty party squirm.
variables: Office Issue: lunch stealing/unwashed dishes/loud phone calls

prompts.title: Funny Resignation Letter (Vent Edition)
prompts.description: The resignation letter you want to write but probably shouldn't.
prompts.text: Write a outrageously funny fictional resignation letter for [Name] leaving [Company]. Include: a faux-formal opener, a hilariously exaggerated list of grievances (endless meetings, the printer that hates them, the mystery smell in the break room), a savage compliment to the CEO, and a dramatic farewell. This is for entertainment only—never actually send.
prompts.usageInstructions: For laughs only. Use the real, professional version when you actually resign.

prompts.title: Excuse Generator for Skipping a Party
prompts.description: Creative (and slightly unbelievable) party excuse templates.
prompts.text: Write 8 hilariously creative yet plausible excuses for skipping [Event Type: office party/family gathering/friend's party]. Include: one fake emergency, one that's technically true, one involving a pet, one involving technology failure, and one that's so absurd they won't know if you're joking. Add one genuinely polite version for good measure.
prompts.usageInstructions: Pick the excuse that fits your personality and don't over-explain it.
variables: Event Type: office party/family gathering/friend's party

prompts.title: Funny Love Letter Using Food Metaphors
prompts.description: Express love entirely through food analogies.
prompts.text: Write a hilariously romantic love letter to [Partner Name] using only food metaphors. Every sentiment must be expressed through food: "You are the cheese to my pizza, the boba to my milk tea, the final slice no one takes because it's too special." Include a paragraph about what kind of meal they are and what kind of dessert the relationship is.
prompts.usageInstructions: Read aloud with a dramatic cooking show accent for maximum comedy.

prompts.title: Fake Horoscope Generator
prompts.description: Hilariously accurate fake horoscopes for friends.
prompts.text: Write a hilariously "accurate" fake horoscope for [Sign] targeting [Friend Name]. Include: a terrifyingly accurate personality roast disguised as cosmic insight, a "lucky number" that references an inside joke, a warning about their most annoying habit, and an absurd prediction for the week ahead that is weirdly plausible.
prompts.usageInstructions: Send anonymously and watch them agonise over its accuracy.

prompts.title: Comedy Roast Opening for a Best Man Speech
prompts.description: A roast-style opening to a best man speech.
prompts.text: Write a 2-minute comedy roast opening for a best man speech at [Groom]'s wedding. The opening should include: a fake compliment followed by a brutal pivot, two wedding-appropriate jokes about the groom's dating history or personality flaws (reference: [Flaw/Story]), and a transition line that pivots gracefully into the sincere part of the speech.
prompts.usageInstructions: Practise the timing of the jokes—silence before the punchline is gold.

prompts.title: Funny Out-of-Office Email Auto-Reply
prompts.description: A hilarious auto-reply for your time away.
prompts.text: Write 3 funny out-of-office auto-reply email templates for [Name] who is away from [Date] to [Date]. Include: one corporate-speak parody (we apologise for the inconvenience of my happiness), one honest version (I'm on a beach and pretending this email doesn't exist), and one that gives ridiculous escalation instructions for emergencies.
prompts.usageInstructions: Check with your company's culture before using the funny version professionally.

prompts.title: Funny Group Chat Name Ideas
prompts.description: Hilarious name options for your WhatsApp group.
prompts.text: Generate 15 hilariously accurate WhatsApp group chat names for a group of [Number] friends who [Shared Trait, e.g., all work in tech/all love food/all complain about adulting]. Include puns, pop-culture references, and at least one name so niche only this group would understand it. Star your top 3.
prompts.usageInstructions: Put it to a group vote—the one with the most laughs wins.
variables: Shared Trait, e.g., all work in tech/all love food/all complain about adulting

prompts.title: Parody Product Review for an Everyday Item
prompts.description: Write a hilariously dramatic Amazon review for an ordinary item.
prompts.text: Write a 5-star parody Amazon review for [Ordinary Item, e.g., a pencil/a spoon/a sock]. Treat the item with the reverence of a life-changing product. Include: a dramatic backstory for how you found it, an emotional journey it took you on, a comparison to your ex who would never understand, and a final conclusion that verges on spiritual.
prompts.usageInstructions: Post as a novelty review on the actual product page for others to enjoy.
variables: Ordinary Item, e.g., a pencil/a spoon/a sock

prompts.title: Love Poem in Sonnet Form
prompts.description: A Shakespearean-style love sonnet for your partner.
prompts.text: Write a Shakespearean sonnet (14 lines, ABAB CDCD EFEF GG rhyme scheme, iambic pentameter) dedicated to [Partner Name]. The theme: the way [their specific quality] makes ordinary moments feel extraordinary. Reference one specific sensory detail (e.g., the way they laugh, their handwriting, the smell of their cooking).
prompts.usageInstructions: Unlock and frame this as a gift alongside a classical book of poetry.

prompts.title: First Date Conversation Starters
prompts.description: Deep, engaging questions for a memorable first date.
prompts.text: Generate 15 first date conversation starters that go beyond "so what do you do?" For [Name] going on a date with someone who loves [Interest]. Include: 5 curious and slightly unexpected questions, 5 light playful starters, and 5 deeper questions that create genuine connection without feeling like an interview. Flag the best 3.
prompts.usageInstructions: Memorise your top 5 so the conversation flows naturally.

prompts.title: Long-Distance Love Letter Series
prompts.description: A 7-part weekly letter series for long-distance couples.
prompts.text: Write 7 short but deeply meaningful weekly love letter drafts for [Name] to send to their long-distance partner [Partner Name]. Each letter (300-400 words) should stand alone but build a cumulative emotional arc. Week 1: what I miss most. Week 2: a memory. Week 3: what I admire. Week 4: a future dream. Week 5: apology and growth. Week 6: gratitude. Week 7: a promise.
prompts.usageInstructions: Personalise and send one each week—physical post for maximum impact.

prompts.title: Relationship Goals Setting Guide for Couples
prompts.description: Set meaningful shared goals as a couple.
prompts.text: Create a relationship goals-setting guide for [Name1] and [Name2]. Cover 5 areas: shared experiences (travel, activities), financial alignment, communication habits, individual growth support, and intimacy and connection rituals. For each area, generate 3 specific goal options at different levels of commitment and provide a 90-day starter action for each.
prompts.usageInstructions: Complete this together over a romantic dinner.

prompts.title: Love Language Discovery Quiz and Guide
prompts.description: Identify your and your partner's love languages.
prompts.text: Create a 20-question love language discovery quiz for [Name] and [Partner]. Based on Gary Chapman's 5 Love Languages framework. After the quiz, provide a results interpretation with specific actionable ways each person can show love in the other's primary language. Include common mismatches and how to navigate them.
prompts.usageInstructions: Both partners should take the quiz separately and then compare results.

prompts.title: Relationship Repair Conversation Guide
prompts.description: Rebuild connection after a prolonged relationship rough patch.
prompts.text: Write a guided conversation framework for [Name1] and [Name2] to use for repairing their relationship after [Time Period] of distance or conflict. Structure: 1) Each partner shares one unspoken feeling (no interruptions), 2) Each names one thing they appreciate about the other, 3) Both identify the patterns that created the distance, 4) Together design 3 new relationship agreements. Provide facilitation notes.
prompts.usageInstructions: Unlock and do this in a neutral, comfortable space—no phones, no distractions.

prompts.title: Cute Daily Text Message Templates for Couples
prompts.description: Keep the spark alive with sweet daily texts.
prompts.text: Generate 30 unique daily text message templates for [Name] to send to [Partner] over one month. Vary the intent each day: morning motivation, midday check-in, evening affirmation, weekend playfulness, and Friday anticipation. Each message should be under 3 sentences and feel personal, not generic.
prompts.usageInstructions: Schedule a few in advance on slow days to maintain consistency.

prompts.title: Love at First Sight Story Prompt
prompts.description: Write the story of how you fell in love.
prompts.text: Write a 500-word creative story about how [Name1] and [Name2] first met and fell in love at [Place] on [Date]. Told from [Name1]'s perspective in first-person narrative. Include: the first sensory impression, the awkward first interaction, the moment something shifted, and end with a line that looks forward. Style: warm, literary, slightly cinematic.
prompts.usageInstructions: Read aloud to your partner on a special occasion.

prompts.title: Valentine's Day Message Pack
prompts.description: 10 unique Valentine's messages for different relationships.
prompts.text: Write 10 unique Valentine's Day messages for different relationship stages and types: 1) Early dating (3 months in), 2) Committed partners, 3) Long-distance, 4) From a husband to wife, 5) From a wife to husband, 6) New parents celebrating their first Valentine's, 7) Friends celebrating Galentine's, 8) A secret admirer, 9) A long-married couple, 10) A hopeful single person's affirmation.
prompts.usageInstructions: Pick the one that matches your stage and personalise the name.

prompts.title: Proposal Speech Script
prompts.description: Pop the question with the perfect words.
prompts.text: Write a marriage proposal speech for [Name] proposing to [Partner Name]. Location: [Location]. Include: a brief story of how you fell in love, 3 specific qualities that made you choose them, the moment you knew they were "the one", and the actual proposal question. End with a contingency line in case of happy tears. Duration: ~2 minutes.
prompts.usageInstructions: Unlock, memorise, and rehearse twice. Then speak from the heart, not the script.

prompts.title: Friend Group Anniversary Tribute
prompts.description: Celebrate how long your friend group has been together.
prompts.text: Write a heartfelt tribute celebrating [Number] years of friendship between [Friend Group Name or list names]. Reference: how you all met, the funniest memory, the hardest moment you got through together, and a toast to the years ahead. Post-worthy and card-worthy.
prompts.usageInstructions: Share in the group chat on the anniversary of when the group formed.
variables: Friend Group Name or list names

prompts.title: Mending a Broken Friendship Letter
prompts.description: Reach out to an old friend after a falling out.
prompts.text: Write a sincere, vulnerable letter from [Name] to their estranged friend [Friend Name] after a falling out [Time Ago] about [Vague Reference to the Issue]. The letter should: acknowledge the hurt without relitigating the fight, express genuine remorse for [Specific Action], affirm the value of the friendship, and extend an invitation to reconnect on their terms, without pressure.
prompts.usageInstructions: Unlock, handwrite, and decide whether to send—sometimes writing it is healing enough.

prompts.title: Best Friend Birthday Toast at a Party
prompts.description: A funny, emotional birthday toast for a best friend.
prompts.text: Write a 3-minute birthday toast for [Name]'s best friend [Friend Name]'s party. Open with a funny story from [Time], pivot to why they are truly exceptional, get slightly emotional about what the friendship means, and close with a roast that brings everyone to tears of laughter. Include a toast line.
prompts.usageInstructions: Practise it so you can deliver it naturally, not reading from your phone.

prompts.title: Friendship Appreciation Message Pack
prompts.description: Tell your friends what they mean to you.
prompts.text: Write 10 unique friendship appreciation messages for [Name] to send to their different friends: one for the friend who always checks in, one for the funny one, one for the wise one, one for the adventurous one, one for the friend who knew you before success, one for the newest friend, one for the oldest friend, one long-distance friend, one friend who supported you in hardship, and one group appreciation.
prompts.usageInstructions: Send one per day for 10 days—randomly and unexpectedly for maximum impact.

prompts.title: Friendship Bucket List — 50 Things to Do Together
prompts.description: Build a bucket list with your best friend.
prompts.text: Create a 50-item friendship bucket list for [Name] and [Friend Name]. Categorise into: local adventures (10 items), travel experiences (10 items), creative projects (10 items), personal growth challenges together (10 items), and silly/fun memories to make (10 items). Tailor to their shared interests: [Interest1] and [Interest2].
prompts.usageInstructions: Print two copies and cross off completed items together.
